topic: What if you could switch off sleep?
part: Chapter 6 of 6: the choice, the ending (long-form, ~47 s)
title: WHAT IF YOU COULD
SWITCH OFF SLEEP?
previous_text: Then your phone rings. Unknown number. Someone's heard about a kid who never sleeps.

script.text: You go up to the roof to think. Sunrise number seven.
Your little sister followed you. She saw the switch. She wants one.
The man on the phone wants one too. For everyone. A whole city that never sleeps.
Four extra months a year, for every person in the city. Factories that never close. Schools that never end. Who'd say no?
Your sister tugs your sleeve. She just wants to stay up for cartoons.
You know what it costs. They don't.
So do you flip it back on, and lose it forever?
Or keep it, and find out what happens on day twelve?
Part one. Tell me what you'd do.

science.claim: Four extra months a year (8 hours a night)
science.working: 8 h x 365 nights = 2,920 h; 2,920 / 24 = 121.7 days, about 4 months
science.source: arithmetic, as in chapter 2; assumes 8 h of sleep a night

science.claim: Day twelve is past the longest monitored stretch awake (about eleven days)
science.working: the 1964 science-fair record was 264.4 h = 11 days 24 min, so day 12 is beyond it
science.source: as in chapter 5 (no real person named)

shots.note: the roof at sunrise, the sun low; you sit alone on the parapet, small against the city; DAY 7 tag
the roof door opens left; your little sister steps out in pajamas, happy, and pads over to you
sis, happy, bouncing on her toes, points at you: she wants one
the man in the suit by the parapet, phone at his ear, lowers it and smiles: for everyone
the whole city: every window snaps on at once, a city that never sleeps
the three of you on the roof, the city behind; windows switch on block by block
over the suit's shoulder onto the glowing city: tags pop OPEN 24/7, SCHOOL NEVER ENDS; he turns to you, hand out: who'd say no?
sis tugs your sleeve, happy; you look down at her
you, worried, eyes still glowing; the music drops away
your hand over the switch, set to OFF, hesitating: flip it back on?
you look into the sun; the string lights and the city die all at once; black, only your glowing eyes
end card on black: what would you do? FLIP IT BACK ON / KEEP IT, then THE END
